report:
Reviewed the complete parse.dependencies claim, all nine implementation entries, and the complete associated test set. Allowed dependencies are source, scope, edition, compilation configuration and generated parse source. Forbidden dependencies are resolved names, checked interfaces, other items' bodies and trait results. The changed local_syms/mods.rs still has a narrow unexpanded_items query: file-backed modules read SourceFile text and scope and call parse_str_to_cst; inline modules receive their parsed children through specify. Expansion/completeness and the now-public symbol_local_item helper share this source file but are not demanded by this parsing path.

parse/mod.rs constructs a Parser from db/source/text/scope and dispatches tree-sitter syntax children. parse/items.rs constructs item identities and CST, reads edition through the owning scope, and consults registered source paths for child modules. Inline child parsing uses the same source with a child scope. These are permitted parse inputs; no resolver or signature query is invoked. Syntax parsing of a function body here is parsing the current module's source, not reading a checked body or another item's semantic body result. parse/attrs.rs reads only syntax plus Configuration.cfgs to evaluate cfg and static inert-attribute classifications. parse/exprs.rs constructs expression/pattern CST and interns literal/name spellings; parse/generics.rs constructs generic bounds/default/where syntax; parse/paths.rs stores path segments/anchors/type arguments without resolution; parse/types.rs constructs type syntax and explicit unsupported/error nodes without lowering semantic types; parse/util.rs interns names and computes relative/absolute source spans. Searches of database/scope call sites and semantic-query calls in these captured parser files found no name resolution, checked signature/body or trait solver demand.

Captured extra dependencies establish that ScopeSymbol lookup walks ownership/edition fields, Name is a text interner, SourceFile is a text/path input, macro token extraction helpers only slice syntax text, and inert attribute helpers use fixed string classification. The Db interface and Database implementation show cfgs as an input and source_file as lookup of registered SourceFile handles. Thus those helper calls do not conceal semantic demand. Macro definitions/invocations are parsed as tokens/paths; selected expansion text is a supplied parse input, not resolved by the parser.

The only associated test is todo::modules_parse_dependencies. Its body explicitly defers a cold input trace, a warm unchanged request with no parse execution, and semantic-only edits preserving parse reuse. It contains no executable assertions, and this report does not call it coverage. Those guarantees require incremental request/edit fixtures and query-event assertions; source inspection alone cannot prove non-execution/backdating across revisions. Retaining this explicit TODO is justified and preserves the verification gap. There are no N/A entries or other associated tests. This review ran review start/read commands only, not behavioral tests, and made no production changes. All current claim aspects are accounted for by inspected implementation plus the visible deferred trace matrix; no new violation or requested edit was found.
